claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 8 years old and lives with you.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask: Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And just to confirm - are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is someone else (such as another parent or family member) already claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Are there any special circumstances I should be aware of? For example:
- Does Alex spend significant time in hospital, care, or living with someone else?
- Is he in any formal care arrangement paid for by the local council?
- Or does he simply live with you full-time at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually... he was in care for a little while. It was a couple of months earlier this year, but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. To understand how this affects your eligibility, I need a bit more detail about the care arrangement.

How long was Alex in care, and approximately when did he return home to live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was about 8 weeks that he was in care, and he came back home a few weeks ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Just one more question about this: While Alex was in care during those 8 weeks, did he spend any regular time at home with you - for example, did he come home for at least 24 hours each week, or for overnight stays?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he didn't come home during that time. He was in care full-time for those 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He was in care for 8 weeks earlier this year but is now back home with you full-time

The key point here is that Alex was in care for exactly 8 weeks. According to the rules, Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks when a child is in care. Since he was in care for exactly that period and is now back home living with you full-time, you should be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

However, it's important to note that you should have informed HMRC about the change in circumstances when Alex went into care. Now that he's back home, if you were receiving Child Benefit that stopped, you may need to contact HMRC to restart it, or if you weren't claiming, you can make a new claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You are **eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex!

If you haven't already claimed or if your payments stopped, you can apply or restart your claim by contacting HMRC or making a claim online. If you have any questions about the application process or need further assistance, feel free to ask!
